{{Nihongo|'''Makoto Fujita'''|藤田 誠|Fujita Makoto}} is a Japanese chemist who specializes in [[supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular]] [[coordination chemistry]]. He is the Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Tokyo]] and a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAAS).<ref name="AAAS">[https://www.tc.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/14950/ Distinguished University Professor Makoto FUJITA Elected Foreign Honorary Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences - 東京カレッジ]</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Emperor Naruhito Empress Masako and Makoto Fujita 20190617.jpg|thumb|left|200px|with [[Emperor Naruhito]] and [[Empress Masako]] (at the Building of Japan Academy on 17 June 2019)]]
He is a professor in the Department of Applied Chemistry at the [[University of Tokyo]]. He has published extensively on the multicomponent assembly of large coordination cages.  Compounds designed and prepared in his research group are variously described as three-dimensional synthetic receptors, coordination assemblies, molecular paneling, molecular flasks, [[crystalline sponges]], and coordination capsules.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Inokuma |first1=Yasuhide |last2=Yoshioka |first2=Shota |last3=Ariyoshi |first3=Junko |last4=Arai |first4=Tatsuhiko |last5=Hitora |first5=Yuki |last6=Takada |first6=Kentaro |last7=Matsunaga |first7=Shigeki |last8=Rissanen |first8=Kari |last9=Fujita |first9=Makoto |date=28 March 2013 |title=X-ray analysis on the nanogram to microgram scale using porous complexes |url=http://www.nature.com/articles/nature11990 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=495 |issue=7442 |pages=461–466 |doi=10.1038/nature11990 |pmid=23538828 |bibcode=2013Natur.495..461I |s2cid=4308105 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Coordination Assemblies from a Pd(II)-Cornered Square Complex|last1=Fujita |first1=Makoto |last2=Tominaga |first2=Masahide |last3=Hori |first3=Akiko |last4=Therrien |first4=Bruno|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|year=2005|volume=38|issue=4 |pages=369–378|doi=10.1021/ar040153h|pmid=15835883 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Functional Molecular Flasks: New Properties and Reactions within Discrete, Self-Assembled Hosts|last1=Yoshizawa |first1=Michito |last2=Klosterman |first2=Jeremy K. |last3=Fujita |first3=Makoto |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |year=2009 |volume=48 |issue=19 |pages=3418–3438 |doi=10.1002/anie.200805340 |pmid=19391140 }}</ref>

He shared the 2018 [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]] with [[Omar Yaghi]] "for conceiving metal-directed assembly principles leading to large highly porous complexes".

[[Hideki Shirakawa]] predicted in 2014 that Fujita would win the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Satoko |last=Ando |url=http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.jp/interview/fujita/ |title=化学の常識を覆した"自己組織化"の未来 |trans-title=The future of “self-assembly” that overturns common sense in chemistry |work=Thomson Reuters |access-date=2014-06-24 |archive-date=2017-07-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703113708/http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.jp/interview/fujita/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

* 2020 – [[Clarivate Citation Laureates|Clarivate Citation Laureate]]
* 2020 – [[Chunichi Culture Award]]
* 2023 – [[Asahi Prize]]<ref name="TOPページ  2023 d895">{{cite web | title=Distinguished Prof. Makoto Fujita has been awarded the Asahi Prize 2022 | website=TOPページ  | date=1 January 2023 | url=https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/news/2023/01/0104.html | access-date=19 November 2023}}</ref>
